content.text: {"what_it_is": {"claims": [{"text": "F-22A (budget line F02200) is a U.S. Air Force aircraft procurement line funded in the Aircraft Procurement, Air Force appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "b5bb3483e72e4fdd"}}, {"text": "The F-22 Raptor is a multi-mission fighter aircraft that combines low observability, supercruise, maneuverability, and integrated avionics to provide air superiority to the Joint Force, access in highly contested environments, and homeland and cruise-missile defense, with a planned service life into the 2040s.", "citation": {"fact_id": "5f7843c57b524cba"}}, {"text": "The force-structure plan comprises 185 aircraft in the F-22 fleet — 32 Block 20 and 153 Block 30/35 by the end of FY 2025 — with an average fleet age of about 17 years, and the program funds planned, incremental modernization of the air vehicle, engine, operational flight program, and training systems.", "citation": {"fact_id": "5f7843c57b524cba"}}, {"text": "One effort within the line procures support equipment for a simulation environment, delivering an F-22 In-a-Box system — including cockpit, hands-on-throttle-and-stick controls, and required software — to the Virtual Test and Training Center at Nellis Air Force Base, Nevada, to operate within the Joint Simulation Environment.", "citation": {"fact_id": "88b1e5869330d93e"}}, {"text": "FY 2026 modification efforts include a Reliability and Maintainability program, Link 16 capability improvement, F119 engine modifications, trainer modernization, Mode 5 identification, sensor enhancement, low-drag tanks and pylons, and a Controlled Reception Pattern Antenna, with two new-start efforts (a Viability modification and a Helmet Mounted Display Cueing System).", "citation": {"fact_id": "b62686233d2a58e6"}}]}, "why_it_matters": {"claims": [{"text": "The program's total funding is $1,077,526 thousand (about $1.08 billion) requested for FY 2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "a48bf05bf0dfe61d"}}, {"text": "In FY 2024 the program recorded actual spending of $348,097 thousand (about $348 million), so the FY 2026 request is roughly three times its recent execution level.", "citation": {"fact_id": "3a69adf72aedb0b6"}}, {"text": "The FY 2026 request splits into a discretionary request of $977,526 thousand (about $978 million) and a reconciliation (mandatory) request of $100,000 thousand (about $100 million).", "citation": {"fact_id": "79c4ed63b170ba67"}}, {"text": "The $100,000 thousand mandatory portion is the reconciliation piece that, combined with the discretionary base, produces the FY 2026 total.", "citation": {"fact_id": "e04bf6a4eeb45f7e"}}, {"text": "Per the program narrative, the mandatory funds would procure 10 Group B Pylon (Active) kits, 3 Group B Pylon (Guard) kits, 10 Group B Tank (Active) kits, and 3 Group B Tank (Guard) kits, with further detail in Section 20007 (Air Superiority) of the Reconciliation Exhibit.", "citation": {"fact_id": "b62686233d2a58e6"}}, {"text": "The FY 2026 request was reduced by $2.201 million for Advisory and Assistance Services in alignment with Executive Order 14222 on government-efficiency cost initiatives.", "citation": {"fact_id": "5f7843c57b524cba"}}]}, "players": {"claims": [{"text": "The program is run by the U.S. Air Force, with funding drawn from the Aircraft Procurement, Air Force appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "5d14b14f58347a8f"}}, {"text": "The research, development, and integration funding underpinning F-22 modernization is carried in a separate program element, PE 0207138F.", "citation": {"fact_id": "5f7843c57b524cba"}}, {"text": "In accordance with Section 1815 of the FY 2008 National Defense Authorization Act (P.L. 110-181), the F-22 is designated as necessary for use by the active and reserve components for homeland defense missions, domestic emergency responses, and military support to civil authorities.", "citation": {"fact_id": "5f7843c57b524cba"}}]}, "recent_developments": {"claims": []}}
